title: Stalks of tensor pullback for a morphism of ringed topoi
statement:
Let $(u,u^\sharp):(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),R)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),S)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], with sites and sheaf values in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $p:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a point (a geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism]), and put $q=u\circ p$ (the composite geometric morphism). For a sheaf $G$ on $\mathcal C$ write $G_p=p^{-1}G$, and similarly write $H_q=q^{-1}H$ on $\mathcal D$. The composition comparison canonically identifies $(u^{-1}H)_p$ with $H_q$, for sheaves of sets, abelian groups and commutative rings, respecting their operations. For every $S$-module sheaf $M$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], put $u^*M=R\otimes_{u^{-1}S}u^{-1}M$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. There is a canonical natural $R_p$-linear isomorphism
$$(u^*M)_p\cong M_q\otimes_{S_q}R_p.$$
Here the ring map $S_q\to R_p$ is the stalk of $u^\sharp$. This comparison sends the stalk of a local pure tensor $r\otimes m$ to $m_q\otimes r_p$, with $m_q$ the image of the inverse-image germ under the composition comparison. It applies termwise to cochain complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] and commutes with their differentials.

proof.text: Construct A=f⁻¹S and its algebraic module lift I using the already proved ringImage and algebraicImage helpers in CochainCompositeConstruction, which reconstruct the finite-product transport on sections. Apply its proved structuralMap helper to bundle I.ringUnderlying.inv followed by f.ringMap as c, using the ring graph equations of f. This is direct reuse of the construction helpers, not an application of the composite existence theorem, and proves the required normalization of c.

proof.text: Take a normalized point presentation a of A at p. Define the composite point t with ring a.ring and modules I.modules followed by a.modules. Its ring identification is p.mapIso(I.ringUnderlying) followed by a.ringUnderlying; its module identification is the corresponding composite natural isomorphism. Apply first the graph equations of I and then those of a to prove every graph equation of t. Naturality and the transported addition graph prove additivity of the composite module functor.

proof.text: Apply the point scalar-extension comparison to c, a and s. Its equivalences evaluated at I(M) give e(M). The ring-map normalization together with I.ringUnderlying.hom followed by c=f.ringMap gives the required normalization of b. Its scalar and module-map equations give linearity and naturality. Cancel I.moduleUnderlying.hom followed by its inverse under p.inverse to identify its generalized-section pure formula with the required composite-point formula.
